title: Metabolic Flexibility of Cutaneous Melanoma Cells Upon Autophagy Modulation: An Immunohistochemical Study
content:
Abstract
Autophagy plays a complex and multifaceted role in melanoma, acting both as a tumor suppressor and as a mechanism supporting tumor cell survival. The metabolic plasticity of tumor cells is closely interconnected with autophagic processes. Despite several therapeutic advances with autophagy-modulating agents, this field remains insufficiently explored. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of autophagy modulators (lithium and chloroquine) on the metabolism of B16 murine melanoma cells. Both agents induced early apoptosis; however, necrosis predominated at the 24-hour time point. Studies in melanoma-bearing mice confirmed that chloroquine suppresses mitochondrial metabolism: expression of IDH3α was reduced twofold, whereas expression of the lactate transporter MCT4 was significantly increased. The mTOR/AKT and SMAD3 signaling pathways were differentially regulated: chloroquine reduced phospho-mammalian target of rapamycin (ph-mTOR) and SMAD3 expression yet increased total protein kinase B (AKT) levels, while lithium exerted a moderate effect on ph-mTOR. These findings suggest that chloroquine likely induces a metabolic shift toward glycolysis, whereas lithium helps maintain oxidative metabolism. The metabolic flexibility of tumor cells characterized in this study provides a strong rationale for combined therapeutic approaches for melanoma.
